newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golds drag Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Golds drag Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: *Stocks close down but rebound off lows, golds lead way lower in battle of miners versus banks. Turnover 251.37 million, A$853.37 million value, 961 traded, 268 steady, 259 up, 434 down.

The Australian stock market closed lower on Tuesday as sliding metal prices pushed the resources sector lower, just offsetting industrial stocks which gained ground due to continued support for the banking sector.
By 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 4.9 points lower at 2285.5. The December share price index was eight points lower at 2300, a 14.5 point premium to the index.
The gold sector led miners down, the gold index losing over three percent after the gold price failed to rebound in Asian markets after passing through US$380 in New York on Monday.
After being quoted at US$378.15/378.65 at New York's close, gold at 0610 GMT was quoted at US$377.90/378.40 in Hong Kong.
"Gold has been the standout, (the gold index) losing over three percent," said broker Justin Hondris of Hartley Poynton.
"Technically, chartists are saying US$380 was the level and it's gone through that. There are a few nerves about where it goes from here."

Highlighting the focus on gold, base metals miners CRA and BHP rebounded strongly off their day's lows to finish at or near square while WMC, with a greater exposure to gold, only just dragged itself off the floor by the close.
Industrial stocks were bolstered by another strong performance from the banks which continued to rise as traders speculated that another interest rate cut could occur as soon as tomorrow.
The Reserve Bank board met on Tuesday, with its monetary policy announcements typically made the next day.

Shares in food group Goodman Fielder topped turnover and ended one cent firmer although no light was shed on buyer/seller identities. Diversified manufacturer GUD Holdings also saw active trade with portfolio repositioning after its cash and scrip bid for appliance maker Sunbeam seen as the likely cause.
In other local markets, Australian bonds remained trapped in a tight range after August retail trade data provided something for both sides of the interest rate cut argument.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.81 percent, up 0.01 from Monday's levels.
The Australian dollar gave an edgy performance as the market fretted over the risk of an imminent rate cut, but such was the uncertainty that dealers felt it better to take cover than take positions.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7910/15, short of Monday's late US$0.7930/35.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures saw active trade as players took up positions in the December contract but options trade was modest.
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 6,582 (7,705)
